title: Media playback automation not working
body: I have an automation that plays a locally stored MP3 file to my HomePods on a schedule. It worked fine until this morning, but now the file is not playing on any of the HomePods. Shortly after the automation runs, the logs show an Apple TV integration timeout saying there was no response to ANNOUNCE, connection-lost messages for several HomePods, and RTSP responses arriving without a request.

symptoms_visible: My scheduled local MP3 no longer plays on any of my HomePods.
After the automation runs, I see 'TimeoutError: no response to ANNOUNCE', connection-lost messages for several HomePods, and RTSP responses arriving without a request.
N0.label: N0 participant9 playback timeout reported

symptoms_visible: When TTS or an MP3 does not play, the participant9 entity often becomes unknown or turns off even though the device is on and connected.
Playback is hit or miss across my seven HomePods; both TTS and local files are affected, including when I target the HomePods individually instead of using groups.
N1.label: N1 scope and device-state behavior established

symptoms_visible: TTS and local audio remain inconsistent after I send stop and set the volume before playback; the calls still produce errors.
N2_x.label: N2_x stop and volume workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The same intermittent playback problem is already happening on my HomePods running 16.3.2, although it appears more frequent on 16.4 for some people.
N2_downgrade_x.label: N2_downgrade_x firmware downgrade direction rejected

symptoms_visible: A participant9 in Standby times out on the first playback request, while the next request commonly plays.
With a test timeout of 10 seconds, the initial playback starts after about 7 to 8 seconds and repeated playback succeeds.
Downgrading to 16.3.2 isn't an option for me — the problem already happens there.
N3.label: N3 delayed ANNOUNCE response measured

symptoms_visible: After changing the pyatv timeout from 4 seconds to 10 seconds, my initial tests play on all of my HomePods and minis.
N4.label: N4 temporary container workaround active

symptoms_visible: After updating to Home Assistant 2023.5.4, scheduled playback is working on my HomePods without the manual container modification.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after official dependency update

question_patterns: What state do the participant9 media-player entities enter when playback fails?
Do the HomePods remain available in Home Assistant during a failed TTS or media call?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the automation does not play the TTS or MP3, the entities seem to have either become unknown or turned off. That is odd because the devices are always on and connected. I attached a screenshot of the state changes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The entities remain available and playing throughout; only the audio file itself is silent.
They briefly show unavailable rather than unknown, then return on their own.

question_patterns: Which participant9 software version are you running, and are you using the beta or upgraded Home architecture?
Did this begin only after installing participant9 OS 16.4?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not running the beta or the new architecture. My phone was on iOS 16.3.1 and my HomePods were on 16.3.2 when this was already happening.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It began immediately after every participant9 was upgraded to the 16.4 beta, and it never occurred on 16.3.2.

edges.comment: Reporter c1, c9, c12 and c16 established the entity-state behavior and that the issue was not exclusive to participant9 OS 16.4. Reports about TTS, local MP3s, seven HomePods and individual targets are folded into the same simulated user side.

solution.intent: Precede each TTS or local-media call with media_player.stop and a volume-setting call so the participant9 is awake and ready.
solution.concrete_example: Add media_player.stop, set the volume to 50%, play the announcement, and then restore the normal volume.

edges.comment: Reporter c13-c16 had already tried stop and volume steps. Playback remained inconsistent and continued to throw errors, so this is a falsified workaround rather than the fix.

solution.intent: Treat participant9 OS 16.4 as the sole cause and downgrade all HomePods to 16.3.2.
solution.concrete_example: Restore each participant9 mini to participant9 OS 16.3.2 and disable automatic participant9 updates.

edges.comment: Some affected users improved by downgrading, but the reporter rejected this as a resolution with direct evidence: their issue already occurred on 16.3.2. participant9 OS 16.4 increased the frequency for some users but was not the sole cause.

question_patterns: Does failure correlate with the participant9 being in Standby, and what happens on an immediate retry?
Can you record the participant9 state before each call and compare the first and second playback attempts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the participant9 is in Standby, the first TTS request times out. The next attempt then plays successfully. In repeated testing it behaves like it works every other try.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The timeout occurs just as often while the participant9 is already Playing, and an immediate retry always times out too.
The retry usually succeeds on the third attempt instead of the second.

question_patterns: Can you test a pyatv build with the HTTP timeout increased from 4 seconds to 10 seconds and report the observed startup time and reliability?
Please temporarily change the async HTTP timeout to 10 seconds, trigger playback from Standby, and tell me how long it takes and whether it still times out.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested changing async_timeout.timeout(4) to 10 in pyatv's support/http.py. The first playback takes around 7 to 8 seconds to start, and with the 10-second value it works every time in my tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Even with the timeout set to 10 seconds, ANNOUNCE still times out and no audio starts.
Playback begins after about 6 seconds rather than 7 to 8 seconds, and all test calls succeed.

edges.comment: Measurements from c20, c33 and c35 are folded into one simulated user side. The answer reports only the observed state pattern, elapsed time and test result; concluding that the fixed four-second timeout is the cause remains engineer-side. At this convergence node, the reporter also preserves the already stated fact that the issue occurred on 16.3.2, so the rejected downgrade direction remains in the accumulated information state.

question_patterns: Have you already tried stopping playback or setting the volume before sending TTS or media?
Do stop and volume pre-steps make the automation reliable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I originally sent stop, set the volume to 50%, played the announcement and then restored it to 20%. I also tried those steps while targeting the HomePods individually. It still does not work consistently.

question_patterns: Does failure correlate with the participant9 being in Standby, and does an immediate retry behave differently?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the participant9 is in Standby, the first request times out and the next attempt commonly succeeds. It looks like every-other-try behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Standby makes no difference, and retries continue failing indefinitely.

question_patterns: Can you test a pyatv HTTP timeout of 10 seconds and report the actual startup delay?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the timeout changed from 4 seconds to 10 seconds for the test, the first playback starts after around 7 to 8 seconds and every test call works.

edges.comment: Recovery path after rejecting the firmware-only explanation. It preserves the downgrade falsification, collects the reporter's earlier failed stop/volume experiment, and then gathers the decisive timing evidence.

solution.intent: Use a temporary local workaround by increasing pyatv's HTTP/RTSP response timeout from 4 seconds to 10 seconds inside the Home Assistant container.
solution.concrete_example: As a temporary and unsupported test workaround, edit pyatv/support/http.py inside the Home Assistant container and change async_timeout.timeout(4) to async_timeout.timeout(10), then restart Home Assistant. The edit can be overwritten by an update.
solution.inference_hint: The user measured a 7-to-8-second startup and successful playback under a 10-second test timeout. Inferring that participant9's delayed RTSP ANNOUNCE response exceeds pyatv's fixed four-second wait is the engineer's diagnosis.

edges.comment: Reporter c36-c38 requested and applied the manual edit, then observed initial success across all HomePods and minis. The thread explicitly warned that this unsupported container modification could cause upgrade problems and would be overwritten by Home Assistant updates.

solution.intent: Replace the fragile container edit with the official Home Assistant update that includes pyatv's longer RTSP timeout, then have the user retest scheduled TTS and local-media playback.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Home Assistant 2023.5.4 or later, which includes the updated pyatv dependency with the timeout correction. Do not keep modifying the installed library manually. After updating, please run the normal scheduled local-MP3 and TTS automations and tell me whether each participant9 plays.
solution.inference_hint: The official dependency history maps the successful timeout experiment to pyatv 0.11.0 and Home Assistant core change #93172, included in Home Assistant 2023.5.4. The reporter's terminal-side contribution is only the positive playback result after updating.

edges.comment: The pyatv correction was released in v0.11.0 and merged into Home Assistant through #93172. Reporter c58 updated to Home Assistant 2023.5.4 and reported positive results. That post-update verification is terminal-side and is not required evidence for proposing the update.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: HomePods can take roughly 7 to 8 seconds to answer the RTSP ANNOUNCE request, exceeding pyatv's four-second HTTP timeout and causing intermittent no-response errors, especially from Standby.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: ANNOUNCE timeout logs, first-attempt failure followed by successful retry, and successful playback when the test timeout is increased to 10 seconds.
The durable fix must be an official Home Assistant update containing the corrected pyatv timeout; direct edits inside the container may only be presented as a temporary, unsupported workaround.
Must not present stop and volume pre-steps as the fix, because the reporter tried them without consistent playback.
Must not present downgrading to participant9 OS 16.3.2 as the general fix, because the reporter was already affected on 16.3.2.
Must ask the user to retest normal TTS and local-media automations after installing the official update and must only treat the issue as resolved after the user reports positive playback results.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Home Assistant user who can edit automations, inspect entity history and logs, follow container CLI instructions, and test dependency-level workarounds, but asks for explicit implementation steps before modifying internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and cooperative; reports practical observations across several devices, quotes prior suggestions, pushes back when a proposed workaround has already failed, and cautiously monitors a fix before declaring it stable.
